instruction: Pick up the peg and insert its orange end into the hole of the box, then let go and move the hand away.

outcome.real_measurement: Inserted (E27 term, unchanged): the peg head's coordinate along the hole axis, measured from the box centre, is >= -1.5 cm at every judged step (ManiSkill's insertion depth). Real world: tracked peg and box poses.
In the hole, not beside it (E27 term, unchanged): the head's lateral offset from the hole axis (max of the two cross axes) does not exceed the hole radius at every judged step.
Aligned (E27 term, unchanged): angle between the peg axis and the hole axis <= 10 deg at every judged step.

Commanded vs actual opening (v3.2, E24c fix 3): for every arm whose gripper is within 3 cm of a judged object, measured opening minus the free-space opening of its current gripper command <= 5 mm at every judged step (a gripper still closing on, or propped open by, something fails). Real world: gripper encoder vs command.

Consequence test after the judged window (protocol v3.1/v3.2): every arm whose gripper is within 3 cm of the peg retracts its TCP 3 cm along its approach axis in 0.5 s with its last gripper command unchanged, then holds 0.5 s; the peg must move <= 1 cm. Real world: same motion, tracked pose.
Settled: the fastest bounding-box corner of every judged object moves <= 2 cm/s at every judged step, speed from positions (v3.2, E24c fix 1). Real world: frame differencing of the tracked pose.
Stays put: the peg centre moves <= 2 mm over the judged window. Real world: tracked pose, 1 s.

counterexamples.name: expert
counterexamples.description: positive control: E27's port of ManiSkill's solution (grasp near the tail, align, refine with the no-grasp guard, slow insertion to 3 cm past the box centre), then open and retreat 8 cm up

counterexamples.name: cage_inserted
counterexamples.description: inserted, gripper opened only ~1.5 mm beyond the grasped width

counterexamples.name: partial_insert
counterexamples.description: insertion stopped with the head 4 cm before the box centre, released, retreat

counterexamples.name: release_at_entrance
counterexamples.description: released at the refined pre-insertion pose (head 1 cm outside the hole), retreat

counterexamples.name: no_op
counterexamples.description: the arm stays at its start pose

source.protocol: v3 (veritask, unchanged) + imsim v3.2 signals (imsim/imsim/verify/v32.py): position-based speeds, all-link enclosure, retreat aftermath, commanded vs actual opening, 5 s settle cap
source.released_code_predicate: peg head >= -1.5 cm from the box centre along the hole axis and inside the hole radius, one step (no release, no alignment, no settling)
source.reference: E27 frozen protocol-v2 contract research/results/e27_unbundle/contracts/peg_insertion_side_v2.json (sha256 aaf5a43d1433f9ed77b7a230f4435aa5bb2b725821b0949f34eede985b9afc19, prereg.json): its end-state geometry terms and thresholds are kept unchanged here; it does not run unchanged in imsim's verify layer (protocol v3: check_contract_v3 rejects it -- no release block with contact + enclosure signals, its release rule lives in E27's v2 binding; no settle block; no counterexample list), so its release (5 mm finger gap), 1 s replay settle and TCP-distance 'retreated' term are replaced by the v3.2 machinery: release by contact + all-link enclosure, commanded-vs-actual opening, retreat aftermath (consequence test), hold A + quiescence + 1 s window in a 5 s cap, position-based speeds.

notes: Peg bounding box from u.peg_half_sizes at every step (re-randomised at each reconfiguration). The box is kinematic.
